title: A baby's signals can mean play, or a need to pause
summary: CDC says to notice a baby's signals: sounds and looking can be an invitation to play, while turning away, yawning, or fussing can mean the baby needs a break.
body: On the CDC 2-month page, caregivers are told to learn the baby's signals in order to know what the baby is feeling and needs. The page's example of wanting to play is making sounds and looking at the person. The example of needing a break is turning the head away, yawning, or becoming fussy. The same note says the caregiver will feel good and the baby will feel safe and loved when those signals are answered. The examples are illustrations. A yawn can also have other causes the page does not list. The tip is not a full code of every cue.
